verses.zh: 以色列人起行，在摩押平原、约旦河东，对着耶利哥安营。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] The Israelites traveled on[NOTE:2] and camped in the rift valley plains[NOTE:3] of Moab on the side of the Jordan River[NOTE:4] across from Jericho.[NOTE:5]
notes: The fifth section of the book (22:1-33:56) traces the Israelite activities in Transjordan. It is hard to determine how long they were in Transjordan, but a good amount of time must have elapsed for the number of moves they made and the wars they fought. There is a considerable amount of information available on this section of the book. Some of the most helpful works include: H. C. Brichto, The Problem of “Curse” in the Hebrew Bible (JBLMS); E. Burrows, The Oracles of Jacob and Balaam; G. W. Coats, “Balaam, Sinner or Saint?” BR 18 (1973): 21-29; P. C. Craigie, “The Conquest and Early Hebrew Poetry,” TynBul 20 (1969): 76-94; I. Parker, “The Way of God and the Way of Balaam,” ExpTim 17 (1905): 45; and J. A. Wharton, “The Command to Bless: An Exposition of Numbers 22:41-23:25, ” Int 13 (1959): 37-48. This first part introduces the characters and sets the stage for the oracles. It can be divided into four sections: the invitation declined (vv. 1-14), the second invitation extended (vv. 15-21), God opposes Balaam (vv. 22-35), and Balaam meets Balak (vv. 36-41).
The verse begins with the vav (ו) consecutive.

The singular form of the word עֲרָבָה (ʿaravah) refers to the rift valley, which extends from Mt. Hermon to the Gulf of Aqaba. In the Bible it most often refers to sections of the rift valley, such as the Jordan valley, the region around the Dead Sea, or the portion south of the Dead Sea. The plural form עַרְבוֹת (ʿarevot) refers to that section of the rift valley which is just north of the Dead Sea. The region is divided by the Jordan river and referred to as the עַרְבוֹת (ʿarevot) of Jericho on the west and the עַרְבוֹת of Moab on the east. Each side has gently sloping plains that go down to the Jordan and the Dead Sea. Jericho’s side descends about 450 feet over five miles, while Moab’s side is steeper. Many versions translate the עַרְבוֹת of Moab simply as “plains of Moab,” but this might be misunderstood as Moab’s tableland above and east of the rift valley.
The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.
For the location of Jericho see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

verses.zh: 以色列人向亚摩利人所行的一切事，西拨的儿子巴勒都看见了。
verses.en: Balak son of Zippor saw all that the Israelites had done to the Amorites.

verses.zh: 摩押人因以色列民甚多，就大大惧怕，心内忧急，
verses.en: And the Moabites were greatly afraid of the people, because they were so numerous. The Moabites were sick with fear because of the Israelites.

verses.zh: 对米甸的长老说：「现在这众人要把我们四围所有的一概餂尽，就如牛餂尽田间的草一般。」那时西拨的儿子巴勒作摩押王。
verses.en: So the Moabites said to the elders of Midian, “Now this mass of people[NOTE:1] will lick up everything around us, as the bull devours the grass of the field.” Now Balak son of Zippor was king of the Moabites at this time.
notes: The word is simply “company,” but in the context he must mean a vast company—a horde of people.

verses.zh: 他差遣使者往大河边的毗夺去，到比珥的儿子巴兰本乡那里，召巴兰来，说：「有一宗民从埃及出来，遮满地面，与我对居。
verses.en: And he sent messengers to Balaam[NOTE:1] son of Beor at Pethor, which is by the Euphrates River[NOTE:2] in the land of Amaw,[NOTE:3] to summon him, saying, “Look, a nation has come out of Egypt. They cover the face[NOTE:4] of the earth, and they are settling next to me.
notes: There is much literature on pagan diviners and especially prophecy in places in the east like Mari (see, for example, H. B. Huffmon, “Prophecy in the Mari Letters,” BA 31 [1968]: 101-24). Balaam appears to be a pagan diviner who was of some reputation; he was called to curse the Israelites, but God intervened and gave him blessings only. The passage forms a nice complement to texts that deal with blessings and curses. It shows that no one can curse someone whom God has blessed.
Heb “by the river”; in most contexts this expression refers to the Euphrates River (cf. NAB, NCV, NRSV, TEV, CEV, NLT).
Heb “in the land of Amaw” (cf. NAB, NRSV, TEV); traditionally “in the land of the sons of his people.” The LXX has “by the river of the land.”
Heb “eye.” So also in v. 11.

verses.zh: 这民比我强盛，现在求你来为我咒诅他们，或者我能得胜，攻打他们，赶出此地。因为我知道，你为谁祝福，谁就得福；你咒诅谁，谁就受咒诅。」
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] now, please come and curse this nation[NOTE:2] for me, for they are too powerful for me. Perhaps I will prevail so that we may conquer them[NOTE:3] and drive them out of the land. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed,[NOTE:4] and whoever you curse is cursed.”
notes: The two lines before this verse begin with the particle הִנֵּה (hinneh), and so they lay the foundation for these imperatives. In view of those circumstances, this is what should happen.
Heb “people.” So also in vv. 10, 17, 41.

The construction uses the imperfect tense אוּכַל (ʾukhal, “I will be able”) followed by the imperfect tense נַכֶּה (nakkeh, “we will smite/attack/defeat”). The second verb is clearly the purpose or the result of the first, even though there is no conjunction or particle.
The verb is the Piel imperfect of בָּרַךְ (barakh), with the nuance of possibility: “whomever you may bless.” The Pual participle מְבֹרָךְ (mevorakh) serves as the predicate.

verses.zh: 摩押的长老和米甸的长老手里拿着卦金，到了巴兰那里，将巴勒的话都告诉了他。
verses.en: So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian departed with the fee for divination in their hands. They came to Balaam and reported[NOTE:1] to him the words of Balak.
notes: Heb “spoke.”

verses.zh: 巴兰说：「你们今夜在这里住宿，我必照耶和华所晓谕我的回报你们。」摩押的使臣就在巴兰那里住下了。
verses.en: He replied to them, “Stay[NOTE:1] here tonight, and I will bring back to you whatever word the Lord may speak to me.” So the princes of Moab stayed with Balaam.
notes: The verb לִין (lin) means “to lodge, spend the night.” The related noun is “a lodge”—a hotel of sorts. Balaam needed to consider the offer. And after darkness was considered the best time for diviners to consult with their deities. Balaam apparently knows of the Lord; he testifies to this effect in 22:18.

verses.zh: 神临到巴兰那里，说：「在你这里的人都是谁？」
verses.en: And God came to Balaam and said, “Who are these men with you?”

verses.zh: 巴兰回答说：「是摩押王西拨的儿子巴勒打发人到我这里来，说：
verses.en: Balaam said to God, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent a message to me, saying,

verses.zh: 『从埃及出来的民遮满地面，你来为我咒诅他们，或者我能与他们争战，把他们赶出去。』」
verses.en: ‘Look, a nation has come out[NOTE:1] of Egypt, and it covers the face of the earth. Come now and put a curse on them for me; perhaps I will be able to defeat them[NOTE:2] and drive them out.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: In this passage the text differs slightly; here it is “the nation that comes out,” using the article on the noun, and the active participle in the attributive adjective usage.
Here the infinitive construct is used to express the object or complement of the verb “to be able” (it answers the question of what he will be able to do).
The verb is the Piel perfect with vav (ו) consecutive. It either carries the force of an imperfect tense, or it may be subordinated to the preceding verbs.

verses.zh: 神对巴兰说：「你不可同他们去，也不可咒诅那民，因为那民是蒙福的。」
verses.en: But God said to Balaam, “You must not go with them; you must not curse the people,[NOTE:1] for they are blessed.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The two verbs are negated imperfects; they have the nuance of prohibition: You must not go and you must not curse.

The word בָּרוּךְ (barukh) is the Qal passive participle, serving here as the predicate adjective after the supplied verb “to be.” The verb means “enrich,” in any way, materially, spiritually, physically. But the indication here is that the blessing includes the promised blessing of the patriarchs, a blessing that gave Israel the land. See further, C. Westermann, Blessing in the Bible and the Life of the Church (OBT).

verses.zh: 巴兰早晨起来，对巴勒的使臣说：「你们回本地去吧，因为耶和华不容我和你们同去。」
verses.en: So Balaam got up in the morning, and said to the princes of Balak, “Go to your land,[NOTE:1] for the Lord has refused to permit me to go[NOTE:2] with you.”
notes: The LXX adds “to your lord.”

The main verb is the Piel perfect, “he has refused.” This is followed by two infinitives. The first (לְתִתִּי, letitti) serves as a complement or direct object of the verb, answering the question of what he refused to do—“to give me.” The second infinitive (לַהֲלֹךְ, lahalokh) provides the object for the preceding infinitive: “to grant me to go.”

verses.zh: 摩押的使臣就起来，回巴勒那里去，说：「巴兰不肯和我们同来。」
verses.en: So the princes of Moab departed[NOTE:1] and went back to Balak and said, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
notes: Heb “rose up.”

verses.zh: 巴勒又差遣使臣，比先前的又多又尊贵。
verses.en: Balak again sent princes,[NOTE:1] more numerous and more distinguished than the first.[NOTE:2]
notes: The construction is a verbal hendiadys. It uses the Hiphil preterite of the verb “to add” followed by the Qal infinitive “to send.” The infinitive becomes the main verb, and the preterite an adverb: “he added to send” means “he sent again.”
Heb “than these.”

verses.zh: 他们到了巴兰那里，对他说：「西拨的儿子巴勒这样说：『求你不容甚么事拦阻你不到我这里来，
verses.en: And they came to Balaam and said to him, “Thus says Balak son of Zippor: ‘Please do not let anything hinder you from coming[NOTE:1] to me.
notes: The infinitive construct is the object of the preposition.

verses.zh: 因为我必使你得极大的尊荣。你向我要甚么，我就给你甚么；只求你来为我咒诅这民。』」
verses.en: For I will honor you greatly,[NOTE:1] and whatever you tell me I will do. So come, put a curse on this nation for me.’”
notes: The construction uses the Piel infinitive כַּבֵּד (kabbed) to intensify the verb, which is the Piel imperfect/cohortative אֲכַבֶּדְךָ (ʾakhabbedekha). The great honor could have been wealth, prestige, or position.

verses.zh: 巴兰回答巴勒的臣仆说：「巴勒就是将他满屋的金银给我，我行大事小事也不得越过耶和华―我　神的命。
verses.en: Balaam replied[NOTE:1] to the servants of Balak, “Even if Balak would give me his palace full of silver and gold, I could not transgress the commandment[NOTE:2] of the Lord my God[NOTE:3] to do less or more.
notes: Heb “answered and said.”
Heb “mouth.”
In the light of subsequent events one should not take too seriously that Balaam referred to Yahweh as his God. He is referring properly to the deity for which he is acting as the agent.

verses.zh: 现在我请你们今夜在这里住宿，等我得知耶和华还要对我说甚么。」
verses.en: Now therefore, please stay[NOTE:1] the night here also, that I may know what more the Lord might say to me.”[NOTE:2]
notes: In this case “lodge” is not used, but “remain, reside” (שְׁבוּ, shevu).
This clause is also a verbal hendiadys: “what the Lord might add to speak,” meaning, “what more the Lord might say.”

verses.zh: 当夜，　神临到巴兰那里，说：「这些人若来召你，你就起来同他们去，你只要遵行我对你所说的话。」
verses.en: God came to Balaam that night, and said to him, “If the men have come to call you, get up and go with them, but the word that I will say to you, that you must do.”

verses.zh: 巴兰早晨起来，备上驴，和摩押的使臣一同去了。
verses.en: So Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the princes of Moab.

verses.zh: 神因他去就发了怒；耶和华的使者站在路上敌挡他。他骑着驴，有两个仆人跟随他。
verses.en: Then God’s anger was kindled[NOTE:1] because he went, and the angel of the Lord stood in the road to oppose[NOTE:2] him. Now he was riding on his donkey and his two servants were with him.
notes: God’s anger now seems to contradict the permission he gave Balaam just before this. Some commentators argue that God’s anger is a response to Balaam’s character in setting out—which the Bible does not explain. God saw in him greed and pleasure for the riches, which is why he was so willing to go.
The word is שָׂטָן (satan, “to be an adversary, to oppose”).

verses.zh: 驴看见耶和华的使者站在路上，手里有拔出来的刀，就从路上跨进田间，巴兰便打驴，要叫它回转上路。
verses.en: And the donkey saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road with[NOTE:1] his sword drawn in his hand, so the donkey turned aside from the road and went into the field. But Balaam beat the donkey, to make her turn back to the road.
notes: The word has the conjunction “and” on the noun, indicating this is a disjunctive vav (ו), here serving as a circumstantial clause.

verses.zh: 耶和华的使者就站在葡萄园的窄路上；这边有墙，那边也有墙。
verses.en: Then the angel of the Lord stood in a path[NOTE:1] among the vineyards, where there was a wall on either side.[NOTE:2]
notes: The word means a “narrow place,” having the root meaning “to be deep.” The Greek thought it was in a field in a narrow furrow.
Heb “a wall on this side, and a wall on that side.”

verses.zh: 驴看见耶和华的使者，就贴靠墙，将巴兰的脚挤伤了；巴兰又打驴。
verses.en: And when the donkey saw the angel of the Lord, she pressed herself into the wall, and crushed Balaam’s foot against the wall. So he beat her again.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “he added to beat her,” another verbal hendiadys.

verses.zh: 耶和华的使者又往前去，站在狭窄之处，左右都没有转折的地方。
verses.en: Then the angel of the Lord went farther, and stood in a narrow place, where there was no way to turn either to the right or to the left.

verses.zh: 驴看见耶和华的使者，就卧在巴兰底下，巴兰发怒，用杖打驴。
verses.en: When the donkey saw the angel of the Lord, she crouched down under Balaam. Then Balaam was angry, and he beat his donkey with a staff.

verses.zh: 耶和华叫驴开口，对巴兰说：「我向你行了甚么，你竟打我这三次呢？」
verses.en: Then the Lord opened the mouth of the donkey, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you have beaten me these three times?”

verses.zh: 巴兰对驴说：「因为你戏弄我，我恨不能手中有刀，把你杀了。」
verses.en: And Balaam said to the donkey, “You have made me look stupid; I wish[NOTE:1] there were a sword in my hand, for I would kill you right now.”
notes: The optative clause is introduced with the particle לוּ (lu).

verses.zh: 驴对巴兰说：「我不是你从小时直到今日所骑的驴吗？我素常向你这样行过吗？」巴兰说：「没有。」
verses.en: The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey that you have ridden ever since I was yours until this day? Have I ever attempted[NOTE:1] to treat you this way?”[NOTE:2] And he said, “No.”
notes: Here the Hiphil perfect is preceded by the Hiphil infinitive absolute for emphasis in the sentence.
Heb “to do thus to you.”

verses.zh: 当时，耶和华使巴兰的眼目明亮，他就看见耶和华的使者站在路上，手里有拔出来的刀，巴兰便低头俯伏在地。
verses.en: Then the Lord opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the Lord standing in the way with his sword drawn in his hand; so he bowed his head and threw himself down with his face to the ground.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hishtaphel verb חָוָה (khavah)— שָׁחָה (shakhah) with metathesis—has a basic idea of “bow oneself low to the ground,” and perhaps in some cases the idea of “coil up.” This is the normal posture of prayer and of deep humility in the ancient religious world.

verses.zh: 耶和华的使者对他说：「你为何这三次打你的驴呢？我出来敌挡你，因你所行的，在我面前偏僻。
verses.en: The angel of the Lord said to him, “Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? Look, I came out to oppose you because what you are doing[NOTE:1] is perverse before me.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your way.”
The verb יָרַט (yarat) occurs only here and in Job 16:11. Balaam is embarking on a foolish mission with base motives. The old rendering “perverse” is still acceptable.

verses.zh: 驴看见我就三次从我面前偏过去；驴若没有偏过去，我早把你杀了，留它存活。」
verses.en: The donkey saw me and turned from me these three times. If[NOTE:1] she had not turned from me, I would have killed you but saved her alive.”
notes: Many commentators consider אוּלַי (ʾulay, “perhaps”) to be a misspelling in the MT in place of לוּלֵי (luley, “if not”).

verses.zh: 巴兰对耶和华的使者说：「我有罪了。我不知道你站在路上阻挡我；你若不喜欢我去，我就转回。」
verses.en: Balaam said to the angel of the Lord, “I have sinned, for I did not know that you stood against me in the road.[NOTE:1] So now, if it is evil in your sight,[NOTE:2] I will go back home.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Balaam is not here making a general confession of sin. What he is admitting to is a procedural mistake. The basic meaning of the word is “to miss the mark.” He now knows he took the wrong way, i.e., in coming to curse Israel.

The reference is to Balaam’s way. He is saying that if what he is doing is so perverse, so evil, he will turn around and go home. Of course it did not appear that he had much of a chance of going forward.
The verb is the cohortative from “return”: I will return [me].

verses.zh: 耶和华的使者对巴兰说：「你同这些人去吧！你只要说我对你说的话。」于是巴兰同着巴勒的使臣去了。
verses.en: But the angel of the Lord said to Balaam, “Go with the men, but you may only speak[NOTE:1] the word that I will speak to you.”[NOTE:2] So Balaam went with the princes of Balak.
notes: The imperfect tense here can be given the nuance of permission.
The Hebrew word order is a little more emphatic than this: “but only the word which I speak to you, it you shall speak.”

verses.zh: 巴勒听见巴兰来了，就往摩押京城去迎接他；这城是在边界上，在亚嫩河旁。
verses.en: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at a city of Moab that was on the border of the Arnon at the boundary of his territory.

verses.zh: 巴勒对巴兰说：「我不是急急地打发人到你那里去召你吗？你为何不到我这里来呢？我岂不能使你得尊荣吗？」
verses.en: Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not send again and again[NOTE:1] to you to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Am I not able to honor you?”[NOTE:2]
notes: The emphatic construction is made of the infinitive absolute and the perfect tense from the verb שָׁלַח (shalakh, “to send”). The idea must be more intense than something like, “Did I not certainly send.” Balak is showing frustration with Balaam for refusing him.
Balak again refers to his ability to “honor” the seer. This certainly meant payment for his service, usually gold ornaments, rings and jewelry, as well as some animals.

verses.zh: 巴兰说：「我已经到你这里来了！现在我岂能擅自说甚么呢？　神将甚么话传给我，我就说甚么。」
verses.en: Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. Now, am I able[NOTE:1] to speak[NOTE:2] just anything? I must speak[NOTE:3] only the word that God puts in my mouth.”
notes: The verb is אוּכַל (ʾukhal) in a question—“am I able?” But emphasizing this is the infinitive absolute before it. So Balaam is saying something like, “Can I really say anything?”

The Piel infinitive construct (without the preposition) serves as the object of the verb “to be able.” The whole question is rhetorical—he is saying that he will not be able to say anything God does not allow him to say.
The imperfect tense is here taken as an obligatory imperfect.

verses.zh: 巴兰和巴勒同行，来到基列・胡琐。
verses.en: So Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath Huzoth.

verses.zh: 巴勒宰了（原文是献）牛羊，送给巴兰和陪伴的使臣。
verses.en: And Balak sacrificed bulls and sheep, and sent some[NOTE:1] to Balaam, and to the princes who were with him.
notes: The understanding is that Balak was making a sacrifice for a covenant relationship, and so he gave some of the meat to the men and to the seer.

verses.zh: 到了早晨，巴勒领巴兰到巴力的高处；巴兰从那里观看以色列营的边界。
verses.en: Then on the next morning Balak took Balaam, and brought him up to Bamoth Baal.[NOTE:1] From there he saw the extent of the nation.
notes: The name Bamoth Baal means “the high places of Baal.”
